name: Google Cloud Vertex AI generative inference
price_basis: USD per 1M TOKENS, representative model Llama 3.3 70B on Vertex AI at $0.72 in / $0.72 out (batch $0.36/$0.36), from cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/pricing fetched 2026-10-16. This confirms the 2026-10-14 OpenRouter Google Vertex row, which was the only place the number lived before. Same page, same day: Llama 4 Scout $0.25/$0.70, Llama 4 Maverick $0.35/$1.15, gpt-oss-120b $0.09/$0.36, DeepSeek-V3.2 $0.56/$1.68, Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 $0.22/$0.88. Vertex prices per model and per SKU (global vs non-global on Gemini); the Llama 3.3 row above is the single on-demand rate published, not a regional matrix.
notes: 2026-10-17: OpenRouter's Google Vertex row for llama-3.3-70b-instruct now publishes a latency cell on the US-flagged row — 1.19s P50, 92 tok/s, still $0.72/$0.72 (a second Vertex row at the same price has no cell). The 2026-10-16 read had no latency cell. measured_* stays the 2026-10-16 Artificial Analysis median (149.9 tok/s, 0.68s first chunk, the lowest TTFT of 11 providers on that page). The OpenRouter P50 of 1.19s / 92 tok/s is a different workload and is not promoted over it; the older OpenRouter 2026-10-14 P50 was 4.44s / 98 tok/s. Price fields stay $0.72/$0.72 from Google's own pricing page. 2026-10-16 refresh. The $0.72/$0.72 price is now sourced from Google's own pricing page, not only from OpenRouter's pass-through row. Measured speed moved: OpenRouter's 2026-10-14 P50 for the Vertex row on llama-3.3-70b was 4.44s latency / 98 tok/s; Artificial Analysis on 2026-10-16 measures Vertex at 0.68s median first chunk (the LOWEST TTFT of 11 providers) and 149.9 output tok/s. Both are kept: the old pair is OpenRouter production traffic, the new pair is AA's benchmark, and the record now carries the third-party measurement because measurement_source is a single enum. Previous measured values: ttft 4440 ms, tps 98. Two services under one endpoint family: first-party Gemini (per-model global/non-global tables, non-global +10%) and the partner-model MaaS catalog where open weights (Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, gpt-oss, Mistral) are served on Google's own infrastructure with Google-set prices. Measured figures are OpenRouter's 2026-10-14 P50 on Google Vertex's llama-3.3-70b endpoint: 98 tok/s but 4.44s latency - the slowest TTFT on that table, an order of magnitude behind Groq, which is the finding that matters for latency-sensitive callers. Vertex also sells tuned-model endpoints at 1.5x base price.
